Playbook.name: Correlation — Remote Execution then LSASS Credential Dump (same host) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: On one host, a remote-execution event was followed within an hour by an LSASS credential-dump event (EQL sequence) - a classic lateral-movement-then-credential-theft chain. Triage: a real attack chain, or coincidental events?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Remote execution then LSASS dump on one host is a high-confidence credential-theft-after-lateral-movement chain.

Assets.AssetType: Correlated across all JCB detection surfaces

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Sysmon process + Windows Security (verified). EQL sequence rule; this playbook confirms both stages and the session linkage.

Signal.Name: Remote Execution then LSASS Credential D
Signal.Details: sequence of remote-exec then LSASS dump on a host.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Confirm the remote-execution-then-LSASS-dump sequence on the host and its scope.

Step.name: Confirm the sequence: remote exec then LSASS access
Step.Purpose: The remote-exec source and the LSASS-access process confirm the credential-theft chain.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("1","4688") AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*lsass*" OR process.parent.name RLIKE "(?i)(wmiprvse|wsmprovhost|psexesvc).*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A remote-exec parent (wmiprvse/psexesvc) then an LSASS-access process is the chain. Confirm the two stages are the same session/account, not coincidental. The account is likely compromised.

Step.name: Where did the remote execution originate
Step.Purpose: The network-logon source identifies the pivoting host to contain.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType == "3" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: The network-logon source before the sequence is the pivoting/attacking host - contain it too.

Node.Condition: A confirmed remote-exec -> LSASS-dump sequence in one session on the host.
Node.Result: True Positive (Lateral Movement + Credential Theft - isolate host + source, IR)

Node.Condition: The two events are coincidental (different sessions/legitimate tools).
A security tool legitimately accessing LSASS after remote admin.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CORR-SEQ, INV-02-CORR-SEQ-SRC to the case.

Indicators.Item: Legitimate remote admin + benign LSASS access.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the events are unrelated; close as false_positive.
Isolate the host AND the source; reset ALL credentials on the host; open IR; hunt the chain on peers.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host and the remote-exec source; reset host credentials.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate host + source; reset all host credentials; open IR; hunt peers.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Credential Guard; restrict lateral protocols; tier admin access.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the two stages are the SAME session/account, not time-coincidence.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host + source isolated; credentials reset; chain hunted.
